strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real limitation of LLM-generated data homogeneity with practical training-free approach applicable to closed-source models
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 diverse tasks with consistent improvements (1.5–3× on Vendi), multiple evaluation metrics, quality assessment, and downstream task evaluation (GSM8K)
Principled mathematical foundation grounding diversity optimization in determinantal point processes and effective rank theory with clear algorithmic instantiation
Solid ablation studies examining key components (DPP explorer selection, textual gradients) with clear demonstration of prompt refinement effectiveness
Computational efficiency analysis with practical improvements over naive DPP sampling; clear algorithmic descriptions with intuitive explorer analogy
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: Lemma 1 uses second-order Taylor approximation with unanalyzed tightness; greedy algorithm for NP-hard MVS problem lacks approximation quality analysis; no empirical validation of theoretical assumptions on real data

Evaluation methodology concerns: same model (GPT-4o mini) used for both generation and evaluation creating potential systematic bias; no human evaluation despite acknowledged importance; quality metric consensus mechanism underspecified

Incomplete experimental analysis: hyperparameter sensitivity largely unexplored (authors acknowledge not investing in parameter tuning); kernel choice weights (0.7/0.3) arbitrary without justification; marginal gain approximation against anchor set not validated for impact

Computational cost not fully transparent: VOYAGER uses significantly more LLM calls (443 vs 50 for sports task) without wall-clock time comparisons; cost-benefit tradeoff incompletely characterized despite practical importance

Limited technical novelty: DPPs for diversity and textual gradients are existing techniques; contribution is primarily engineering-focused combination for iterative dataset generation, somewhat incremental

Reproducibility concerns: relies on proprietary GPT-4o mini model; hyperparameters incompletely specified; no code availability mentioned; ablation limited to two main studies; no analysis of failure modes or task characteristics determining method effectiveness

strengths: Well-grounded theoretical motivation using determinantal point processes with connection to effective rank and volume
Training-free method works with closed-source models—significant practical advantage over post-training approaches
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 diverse tasks with multiple metrics (Lexical, Cosine, Vendi) and quality assessment
Strong empirical results: 296% Vendi improvement over baseline on creative tasks, 412% on reasoning tasks, with quality preservation
Practical downstream validation: 28% improvement on GSM8K (35.7→45.7 for Gemma-7B) demonstrates real utility
Thorough ablations demonstrating importance of both DPP-based explorer selection and textual gradients
Clear presentation with intuitive explorer analogy and well-specified algorithms
weaknesses: Theoretical approximations lack rigor: Lemma 1 uses Taylor approximations with 'roughly approximated' language; no error bounds or conditions for when approximation holds; connection between maximizing anchor set volume and full dataset diversity not formally justified

Evaluation bias: diversity metrics (Vendi, cosine similarity) directly measure the volume objective, making VOYAGER appear more favorable; lacks human evaluation of diversity perception and quality despite acknowledging this limitation

Limited algorithmic novelty: combines existing DPP machinery (Kulesza et al., 2012) with textual gradients (Pryzant et al., 2023); distinguishing contribution from concurrent work (Chen et al., 2025) on determinant-based post-training needs clarification
Marginal gain computation biased: computing only w.r.t. fixed-size anchor set rather than full dataset introduces unknown bias; a dataset could be diverse locally but redundant globally

Experimental scope limitations: tasks limited to text generation; downstream validation only on GSM8K; hyperparameter sensitivity (τ, k, b) largely unexplored; kernel choice (0.7/0.3 RBF/Jaccard) appears arbitrary without ablation

LLM call efficiency trade-off underexplored: uses 3-10x more calls than simple baselines (50→400-700), which may be prohibitive for cost-conscious users; relationship between threshold τ and acceptance rate ζ not characterized
No statistical significance testing: standard deviations reported but some quality metric improvements fall within noise; no Bonferroni corrections
Reproducibility concerns: depends on closed-source GPT-4o mini and OpenAI embeddings; no mention of code release; some hyperparameters (Algorithm 5 α parameter) lack justification

strengths: Addresses timely and important problem of synthetic data diversity from LLMs with clear motivation
Principled mathematical grounding in DPPs with clear algorithm formulation and complexity analysis
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 tasks with multiple diversity metrics (cosine, lexical, Vendi) and human evaluation (good inter-annotator agreement)
Strong and consistent empirical results (1.5-3× diversity improvement) with no significant quality degradation
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (diverse explorers, textual gradients, length effects)
Demonstrated downstream benefit: 35.7%→45.7% on GSM8K (Gemma-7B), showing practical utility
Training-free and compatible with closed-source models (no parameter access needed)
Clear presentation with helpful algorithms, figures, and extensive appendices
weaknesses: Theoretical approximations are loose: Lemma 1 works well only for uniform eigenvalue distributions, no convergence guarantees, anchor set approximation impact unexplored
High computational cost (8-14× more LLM calls than baselines: 400-700 vs 50 for 500 samples) limits practical applicability despite strong diversity gains
Heavy dependency on proprietary models (OpenAI embeddings and LLMs) creates reproducibility concerns and circular evaluation using only OpenAI models
Critical design choices under-justified: kernel weights (0.7/0.3 RBF/Jaccard) and anchor set size (k=10) lack sensitivity analysis or principled selection
Incomplete diversity characterization: paper acknowledges lack of comprehensive analysis of diversity types; unclear whether gains are semantic or length-driven (Table 5 shows length confound)
Limited downstream evaluation: only GSM8K with small models (Gemma 2B/7B); no evaluation on other task types (NLU, classification) or larger models
Textual gradient component under-analyzed: relies on LLM refinement quality but limited empirical validation beyond rejection rate plots
Missing statistical significance testing despite overlapping confidence intervals on some metrics
No evaluation on open-source LLMs; results may not generalize beyond proprietary models
Hyperparameter choices appear ad-hoc (e.g., author notes 'we did not invest effort in finetuning parameters like τ') despite being critical to performance
